topics.label: Diversity of living and non-living things: characteristics of living things
Classification of living things: plants (flowering/non-flowering), animals, fungi, bacteria
topics.note: Classify from observable features in tables and pictures; recall of individual species is not required.

topics.label: Diversity of materials: types and properties (strength, flexibility, waterproof/absorbent, allowing light through, floating and sinking)
Life cycles of plants: observing and comparing stages (seed, young plant, adult plant, flowers, fruits)
topics.note: Germination conditions and seed parts are P5 under the current syllabus and are not assessed here.

topics.label: Life cycles of animals: three- and four-stage cycles, frog, mosquito control
Properties of magnets: magnetic materials, poles, attraction and repulsion, force through materials
Making and using magnets: stroke and electrical methods, temporary/permanent magnets, uses
Open-ended explanations using claim, evidence and reasoning
topics.note: Schools assess written explanations; the app uses objective items only (Functional Design §1).

topics.label: Practical test: observing, measuring, classifying with real materials
topics.note: Hands-on practical assessment stays outside the app.

topics.label: P4 lower-block topics (plant and human systems, matter, light, heat)
topics.note: Taught in P4 under the 2023 syllabus; outside Pilot Science scope.

limitations: Primary Science starts at P3; there is no P2 Science course.
Pilot release: first two topics (living/non-living, classification) at the 75% guideline, computed only from reviewed leaves; the other five unlock in syllabus order.
Leaves are an author working map (one per knowledge point plus deferred/external leaves) and need independent page verification before any coverage figure is computed.
Teaching cards use static observation diagrams and tables; short animations named in the design are not yet authored.
Some schools assess magnets in P4; the syllabus places making magnets by stroking and by electricity in P3 (PDF p63).
